Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:28:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike - impacting checkout throughput

Chloe / team — initial findings (rapid):

- Observed: sharp latency tail and 5xx spike on route /v1/generate/checkout between 07:48–08:20 PDT. Token queue depth increased on GPU pool redwood-dedicated-03.
- Hypothesis: KV-cache hotshot + degraded batching on one dedicated node causing increased host CPU and request retries, cascading into higher p99 and some 500s from model runtime timeouts. Not seeing a model accuracy regression.
- Evidence: correlated p99 increase with host-level CPU at 92% and a series of kernel timeouts in the runtime logs (attached excerpt).

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Evacuate traffic from redwood-dedicated-03 to redwood-dedicated-07 (fast, expected partial recovery in ~6 min).
2) Temporarily reduce maximum batch size on the affected pool (low risk, reduces throughput but reduces latency).
3) Roll back recent kernel selection tweak (higher risk, needs 25+ min to validate).

I'll attempt option 1 now and will report back. Creating a short-run checklist and will post into the war-room.

From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:48:02 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production latency & 5xx spike - impacting checkout throughput

Sabrina — quick customer-facing summary and next steps. First, sincere apologies for the impact and thanks for the log bundle — that helped accelerate our triage.

What happened (summary):
- Start: ~07:48 PDT — increased p99 latency and a rise in 5xxs on /v1/generate/checkout.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): runtime-level kernel scheduling + a KV-cache hotkey pattern degraded a single dedicated node (redwood-dedicated-03), increasing CPU and token queueing, which caused timeouts and elevated 500s.

What we did (timeline):
- 08:29 PDT: Evacuated traffic from redwood-dedicated-03 to redwood-dedicated-07.
- 08:35 PDT: Applied temporary batch-size reduction on affected pool to reduce tail latency.
- 08:50 PDT: Observed progressive recovery of throughput; checkout success rate improving toward baseline.

Current status (11:48 PDT):
- Throughput: ~92% of baseline (improving).
- 5xx rate: down from peak 4.8% to 0.7% (target <0.5%).
- Latency: p50/p95 returned close to expected; p99 still slightly elevated.

Next steps and customer asks:
- We will keep the traffic split and small batch-size in place for another 90 min while we monitor telemetry.
- Infra will run a controlled kernel-selection rollback candidate in staging; if validated, we'll schedule a safe rollback outside of peak hours.
- We will provide a consolidated post-incident report (root cause, timeline, remediation, and KPI impact) within 48 hours.

SLA note: We will assess whether the event meets SLA credit thresholds and coordinate via your procurement contact — we'll include that in the post-incident report.

If you need a separate exec briefing for your leadership, we can schedule immediately. Thank you for the fast signals — please let us know if you see any residual problems.

Best,
-Chloe
